extracted.intended_audience: researchers and peer-review stakeholders (conference organizers, editors, meta-reviewers) studying review quality
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines, metrics, and experimental protocols for measuring and analyzing the quality of peer reviews (evaluations of paper reviews) in a conference setting, including questionnaire items, bias checks, agreement/miscalibration metrics, and statistical tests. Focused on conference peer review but applicable to similar review-evaluation contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall quality score (7-point)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluators were asked to rate the overall quality of paper reviews on a 7 point scale. Higher ratings correspond to higher rated quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the primary aggregate outcome of perceived review quality. Distribution was symmetric around median score 4. The overall score is analyzed alongside the four specific criteria and is used in RCT and bias analyses (e.g., Mann-Whitney U τ statistic comparisons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The review demonstrates an adequate understanding of the paper." Evaluated on a 5-point Likert scale ranging from -2 (Strongly Disagree) to 2 (Strongly Agree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of four itemized criteria (derived from Review Quality Indicators) used to capture specific aspects of review usefulness. Criteria scores are analyzed individually and mapped to overall scores in the subjectivity/commensuration analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The review covers all the required aspects." Evaluated on a 5-point Likert scale ranging from -2 (Strongly Disagree) to 2 (Strongly Agree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a core criterion; in the RCT on elongation Coverage showed the strongest effect of length. See S1 Appendix for full questionnaire wording and additional explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiation (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Evaluations made in the review are well supported." Evaluated on a 5-point Likert scale ranging from -2 (Strongly Disagree) to 2 (Strongly Agree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures whether claims in the review are justified with evidence or reasoning. Analyzed separately for bias and mapping to overall score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructiveness (criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The review provides constructive feedback to authors." Evaluated on a 5-point Likert scale ranging from -2 (Strongly Disagree) to 2 (Strongly Agree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures usefulness and actionability of feedback; included in criteria-to-overall mapping and bias analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uselessly elongated review bias (length bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: The hypothesis and measured phenomenon that adding large amounts of non-informative text to a review (increasing length without improving substantive content) can spuriously increase perceived review quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCT design: selected 10 reviews, created 'long' versions by adding filler (repeat headers, replicate abstract, repeat summary, write out multiple-choice text), randomly assigned evaluators to long vs short conditions. Statistical analysis uses a Mann-Whitney U-derived τ statistic, bootstrap (20,000 iterations) for CIs, and Fisher permutation test (20,000 permutations). Results: long reviews scored significantly higher (τ≈0.64 overall; mean overall 4.29 vs 3.73), with strongest effect on Coverage (τ≈0.71).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' outcome-induced bias (positivity bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors evaluating reviews show a positive bias toward reviews that recommend acceptance of their own papers versus those recommending rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-parametric matched-pairs analysis: match pairs of evaluations by the same author on the same paper where one review is 'accept' and one 'reject' controlling for length (≤1.5×) and similarity in non-author mean scores (within 1 point) and minimum non-author evaluations (≥2). Test via Mann-Whitney U τ statistic with bootstrapped CIs and Fisher permutation. Result: strong positive bias (τ≈0.82; accept reviews ≈1.41 points higher on 7-point scale).

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching criteria for paired comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria used to pair reviews for fair comparisons (e.g., in authors' bias analysis): (i) evaluation done by same author on same paper; (ii) pair of reviews have similar length (longer ≤1.5× shorter); (iii) both reviews have at least 2 evaluations from non-authors and have received a mean overall evaluation score within 1 point of each other from non-authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These matching constraints are designed to control for author/paper heterogeneity, length confounding (per RCT), and proxy for true quality (non-author mean). Used to form n=418 matched pairs for the authors' bias test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-evaluator agreement / disagreement rate
rubrics_metrics.description: A measure of consistency: for any pair of evaluators and any pair of reviews both evaluated by them, they 'agree' if both score the same review higher than the other; they 'disagree' if the reviewers' orderings are opposite; ties are discarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute total agreements and disagreements across all evaluator-review pairs. Report ties (e.g., 29% ties for overall score, 37–40% ties for criteria) and disagreement rates (≈0.3 across criteria). Compare to random baseline (0.5) and historical paper-review disagreement (NeurIPS 2016).

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscalibration (linear evaluator-offset model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modeling evaluators' miscalibration as an additive offset: y_ij = f_i + b_j + ε_ij, where f_i ~ N(μ, α_f) is objective quality, b_j ~ N(0, α_b,t) is evaluator offset (per evaluator type t), and ε_ij ~ N(0, σ^2) is idiosyncratic noise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fit via Gaussian process regression / maximum likelihood (GPy). The evaluator-offset variance α_b,t (normalized by α_f) quantifies degree of miscalibration per evaluator type (meta-reviewer, reviewer, author, external). Larger α_b,t implies more miscalibration. Reported normalized values (e.g., authors' α_b ≈0.780 vs ~0.43–0.46 for others) and compare to prior NeurIPS results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjectivity / commensuration bias (criteria-to-overall mapping variability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjectivity measured as variability in how evaluators map individual criterion scores (Understanding, Coverage, Substantiation, Constructiveness) to an overall quality score — i.e., differing weights/priorities among evaluators (commensuration bias).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn a monotonic function mapping criteria scores to overall scores (ensuring improvement in any one criterion doesn't decrease overall). The degree to which individual evaluators or groups differ from the learned mapping (e.g., via loss or variance) quantifies commensuration bias. Note that other sources of subjectivity may exist (unobserved criteria) and should be acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonic mapping learning (criteria → overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn a mapping from the multi-dimensional criteria scores to the scalar overall score under the monotonicity constraint (improvement in any criterion holding others constant should not decrease overall score).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to (i) predict overall scores from criteria, (ii) analyze subjectivity by measuring residuals or variability in mappings across evaluators, and (iii) quantify how much arbitrariness arises from differing commensuration functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study recruitment and evaluator-role definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of evaluator roles and recruitment protocol: Meta-Reviewers (evaluate reviews on one paper from own pool), Paper Reviewers (evaluate other reviewers' reviews on a paper they reviewed), Paper Authors (evaluate reviews on up to 2 of their own papers), External Reviewers (evaluators asked to evaluate reviews on one paper they did not handle). Recruitment was opt-in, voluntary, with informed consent, conducted via conference management platform during review period before final decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes populations whose evaluations were compared and modeled separately; miscalibration parameters are per-role. Participation timing and privacy (cloud storage of reviews; deletion later) affect feasibility and ethics of replicating similar studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elongation strategies to alter review length without improving substantive content
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete methods used to create 'uselessly elongated' reviews while retaining underlying quality: repeating the text box header as introductory sentence, repeating the summary in other sections, writing out text from multiple-choice questions in text boxes, replicating the abstract in summary or body text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are example anti-pattern manipulations demonstrating how review length can be increased without adding informative content; careful manual construction is needed to avoid improving true review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical testing protocol (RCT and comparisons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of non-parametric Mann-Whitney U-derived τ statistic to compare distributions (interpretable as probability one condition scores higher than the other), bootstrap for confidence intervals (20,000 iterations), and Fisher permutation testing (20,000 permutations) to obtain p-values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: τ=0.5 is null for no effect (for pairwise comparisons). Bootstrapping done within-review to preserve structure. Permutation tests permute evaluators within each review preserving group sizes. This protocol is used for RCT length bias and authors' bias analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of non-author evaluations as proxy for 'true' quality
rubrics_metrics.description: When true objective quality of a review is unknown, the mean evaluations from non-authors (meta-reviewers, reviewers, external reviewers) are used as a proxy to control for underlying review quality in matching and analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied in matching criteria (require both reviews to have at least 2 non-author evaluations and mean overall scores within 1 point). This is an explicit methodological choice to reduce confounding when estimating author-specific biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questionnaire design based on Review Quality Indicators (RQIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection and tailoring of a concise set of review-evaluation criteria drawn from proposed Review Quality Indicators (RQIs) to suit machine-learning conference papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study explicitly chose four criteria for brevity and relevance; full questionnaire and item explanations are available in S1 Appendix. The authors note potential limitations from modifying RQI (e.g., re-validation may be warranted when transferring RQIs across domains).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie handling in pairwise agreement computations
rubrics_metrics.description: When computing pairwise agreement/disagreement between evaluators on a pair of reviews, ties are discarded (not counted as agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ties accounted for separately (reported percentages). This affects the denominator when reporting agreement/disagreement rates and should be made explicit in analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and data-sharing constraints for human-subjects review-evaluation data
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical constraint: raw evaluation data from human subjects may be sensitive (e.g., evaluators fearing retaliation) and cannot always be shared; consent forms may promise non-distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors provided partially aggregated data and deposited it in a public repository (OSF) that preserves participant privacy per consent. Any replication or reuse must respect consent agreements and consider thorough anonymization.
